claims.claim: In Nguyen and colleagues' human evaluation at temperature 3 with the lower-diversity setting, min-p stories scored 7.74 out of 10 for quality against 5.75 for top-p and 6.75 for standard sampling.
claims.source: Nguyen Nhat Minh, Andrew Baker, Clement Neo, Allen Roush, Andreas Kirsch and Ravid Shwartz-Ziv, 'Turning Up the Heat: Min-p Sampling for Creative and Coherent LLM Outputs', ICLR 2025 (arXiv v8, 20 Nov 2025)
claims.page: Table 4 (row T=3, Quality, Lower Diversity Settings)

claims.claim: Nguyen and colleagues report min-p winning 56.54 percent on the AlpacaEval Creative Writing benchmark at temperature 1.5, against 53.18 percent for temperature-only sampling.
claims.source: Nguyen Nhat Minh, Andrew Baker, Clement Neo, Allen Roush, Andreas Kirsch and Ravid Shwartz-Ziv, 'Turning Up the Heat: Min-p Sampling for Creative and Coherent LLM Outputs', ICLR 2025 (arXiv v8, 20 Nov 2025)
claims.page: Table 3b (AlpacaEval Creative Writing % win, column tau=1.5)

claims.claim: Nguyen and colleagues concede that their human evaluation rests on a limited sample size and gives directional insight rather than a settled result.
claims.source: Nguyen Nhat Minh, Andrew Baker, Clement Neo, Allen Roush, Andreas Kirsch and Ravid Shwartz-Ziv, 'Turning Up the Heat: Min-p Sampling for Creative and Coherent LLM Outputs', ICLR 2025 (arXiv v8, 20 Nov 2025)
claims.quote: this represents a limited sample size, it provides valuable directional insights

claims.claim: Nguyen and colleagues relay, from Ilya Gusev's run of Sam Paech's EQ-Bench Creative Writing benchmark, a min-p score of 62 at temperature 1.5 against the baseline's 51.5 at temperature 1.0.
claims.source: Nguyen Nhat Minh, Andrew Baker, Clement Neo, Allen Roush, Andreas Kirsch and Ravid Shwartz-Ziv, 'Turning Up the Heat: Min-p Sampling for Creative and Coherent LLM Outputs', ICLR 2025 (arXiv v8, 20 Nov 2025)

claims.claim: Basu and colleagues measured that sentence-level repetition in GPT-2 output effectively disappears above an observed cross-entropy of about 2.5.
claims.source: Sourya Basu, Govardana Sachitanandam Ramachandran, Nitish Shirish Keskar and Lav R. Varshney, 'Mirostat: A Neural Text Decoding Algorithm that Directly Controls Perplexity', ICLR 2021 (arXiv v2, 14 Jan 2021)
claims.quote: beyond a threshold of cross-entropy, which seems to be around 2.5

claims.claim: Basu and colleagues measured that human-written continuation settles at a limiting cross-entropy rate as it lengthens, falling into neither the boredom nor the confusion trap.
claims.source: Sourya Basu, Govardana Sachitanandam Ramachandran, Nitish Shirish Keskar and Lav R. Varshney, 'Mirostat: A Neural Text Decoding Algorithm that Directly Controls Perplexity', ICLR 2021 (arXiv v2, 14 Jan 2021)

claims.page: section 5.3, Boredom and Confusion Traps, discussion of Figure 5c

claims.claim: Basu and colleagues report that at a target cross-entropy of 3 more than half their raters guessed the AI-generated text was human-written.
claims.source: Sourya Basu, Govardana Sachitanandam Ramachandran, Nitish Shirish Keskar and Lav R. Varshney, 'Mirostat: A Neural Text Decoding Algorithm that Directly Controls Perplexity', ICLR 2021 (arXiv v2, 14 Jan 2021)
claims.quote: more than half of raters mistakenly guessed the AI-generated text

claims.claim: Basu and colleagues measured that GPT-2-XL at 1558 million parameters repeats slightly less than GPT-2 at 117 million parameters at the same observed cross-entropy.
claims.source: Sourya Basu, Govardana Sachitanandam Ramachandran, Nitish Shirish Keskar and Lav R. Varshney, 'Mirostat: A Neural Text Decoding Algorithm that Directly Controls Perplexity', ICLR 2021 (arXiv v2, 14 Jan 2021)
claims.quote: have slightly less repetitions for a fixed value of cross-entropy

claims.claim: Su and colleagues measured cosine similarities above 0.95 between the representations of different tokens within a single sentence in GPT-2.
claims.source: Yixuan Su, Tian Lan, Yan Wang, Dani Yogatama, Lingpeng Kong and Nigel Collier, 'A Contrastive Framework for Neural Text Generation', NeurIPS 2022 (arXiv v3, 26 Sep 2022)
claims.quote: the cosine similarities between tokens within a sentence are over 0.95

claims.claim: Su and colleagues ran their whole degeneration evaluation on the Wikitext-103 test set, that is on encyclopedic prose.
claims.source: Yixuan Su, Tian Lan, Yan Wang, Dani Yogatama, Lingpeng Kong and Nigel Collier, 'A Contrastive Framework for Neural Text Generation', NeurIPS 2022 (arXiv v3, 26 Sep 2022)
